title: Earth Watch
subtitle: Global Wildfire & Land Surface Monitor
briefing: Design and launch an operational Earth observation observatory to track wildfire propagation, deforestation, and agricultural water usage across continental biomes. The mission demands consistent sun-synchronous lighting, multi-spectral capability, and high data downlink throughput.
requirementsList: Ground Optical Spatial Resolution <= 30 m
Full Global Surface Revisit <= 16 days
Mission Operational Design Life >= 5.0 years
Daily Science Data Return Fraction >= 90%
Total Project Lifecycle Cost within Budget Cap ($235M)
Flight Readiness Delivery within Schedule Deadline (54 mo)
realWorldContext: Landsat 8 and 9 orbit in a 705 km sun-synchronous orbit, repeating their exact orbital ground track every 16 days with an 8-day offset between the two satellites, imaging Earth's continents in 30-meter multispectral and 100-meter thermal infrared.

title: Exoplanet Hunter
subtitle: All-Sky Stellar Transit Survey
briefing: Deploy a wide-field photometric observatory to discover transiting exoplanets around bright nearby stars across the entire celestial sphere. The mission requires an expansive field of view, sub-arcminute pointing stabilization, and an unocculted viewing geometry with >90% observing efficiency.
requirementsList: Combined Optical Field of View >= 2,000 deg²
ADCS Boresight Pointing Stability <= 0.01°
Science Observing Viewing Efficiency >= 90%
Mission Operational Design Life >= 2.0 years
Periodic Science Downlink Buffer Resolution Each Orbit
Total Project Lifecycle Cost within Budget Cap ($210M)
Flight Readiness Delivery within Schedule Deadline (48 mo)
realWorldContext: TESS utilizes a unique P/2 lunar-resonant 13.7-day high Earth orbit (108,000 x 375,000 km). This orbit keeps the spacecraft outside Earth's radiation belts and shadow for continuous photometric observations, downlinking data during rapid perigee passes.

title: Space Weather Sentinel
subtitle: Sun-Earth L1 Solar Storm Warning
briefing: Station an early-warning heliophysics platform at the Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange point (1.5M km upstream) to provide real-time alerts of coronal mass ejections and solar energetic proton storms.
requirementsList: Stationed in continuous Sun-Earth L1 Halo Orbit
Continuous Real-time Solar Wind Magnetometer & Plasma Telemetry
High Radiation Hardness (TID >= 100 krad)
Uninterrupted Deep Space Network Telemetry Link
realWorldContext: Satellites at L1 observe the solar wind ~15 to 45 minutes before it impacts Earth's magnetosphere, giving critical warning to electrical grids and astronaut crews.

title: Cosmic Origins Observatory
subtitle: Cryogenic Sun-Earth L2 Deep Space Observatory
briefing: Deploy an infrared space observatory to the Sun-Earth L2 Lagrange point to peer 13.5 billion years into cosmic history and characterize exoplanet atmospheres. Requires deep cryogenic cooling (<50K) and sub-arcsecond star tracking.
requirementsList: Insertion into Sun-Earth L2 Quasi-Periodic Halo Orbit
Cryocooler Active Thermal Cooling Support for Near-IR Payloads
ADCS Precision Pointing Accuracy <= 0.005°
Radiation Hardened Avionics for Deep Space Cruise
realWorldContext: At Sun-Earth L2, Earth, Sun, and Moon are perpetually located in the same hemisphere, allowing a single multi-layer sunshield to protect the telescope from both direct solar irradiance and terrestrial thermal glow.

title: Global Telecom Relay
subtitle: Geostationary High-Throughput Orbital Node
analogue: NASA Tracking and Data Relay Satellite (TDRS)
briefing: Place a heavy-capacity communication satellite into geostationary orbit to provide continuous high-throughput Ku/Ka-band links for human spaceflight missions and remote science assets.
requirementsList: Geostationary Equatorial Orbit (35,786 km, 0° inclination)
High-Power Solar Array Generation >= 1500 W
Station-Keeping Propellant Budget for >= 10.0 Year Operational Life
Continuous Dedicated Ground Network Link
realWorldContext: Geostationary communication satellites require approximately 1,500 m/s of delta-V from standard transfer orbit to circularize and adjust orbital inclination to zero.

title: Lunar Pathfinder
subtitle: Polar Volatiles & Topographic Mapping
briefing: Insert a high-inclination reconnaissance spacecraft into a low circular orbit around the Moon to locate water ice in permanently shadowed polar craters and certify Artemis landing sites.
requirementsList: Low Circular Lunar Polar Orbit (100 km, 90°)
Sub-meter Landing Site Imagery
Frequent Mascon Gravitational Station-Keeping Maneuvers
Farside Data Recording Buffer During Earth Blackouts
realWorldContext: LRO has mapped the lunar surface for over a decade from a 50-100 km polar orbit, braving extreme thermal swings between lunar noon and night.

title: Artemis Shackleton Lander
subtitle: Lunar South Pole Powered Descent
briefing: Execute a trans-lunar trajectory, polar lunar insertion, and closed-loop powered descent to soft-land scientific instruments near Shackleton Crater at the lunar South Pole.
requirementsList: High-Thrust Propulsion Sizing for Powered Lunar Deceleration
Cryogenic Thermal Insulation for Polar Night Shadow Survival
Direct Earth High-Gain X/Ka Telemetry Antenna
Total Project Cost under $220M Funding Cap
realWorldContext: Soft-landing on the Moon requires complete elimination of 1.7 km/s orbital velocity using rocket propulsion with zero atmospheric drag assistance.

title: Red Planet Relay
subtitle: Mars Orbital Science & Surface Communications Hub
briefing: Journey across interplanetary space to Mars, execute an aerocapture or propulsive capture into Low Mars Orbit, and operate as a high-bandwidth telecommunications relay for surface rovers.
requirementsList: Trans-Mars Injection (TMI) and Mars Orbit Insertion (MOI)
Massive Solar Array Sizing for 586 W/m² Solar Irradiance
Deep Space Network Telecommunications with 20-min Latency
Dual Science Imaging and Surface UHF Rover Relay Payload
realWorldContext: Mars orbiters require autonomous fault management due to the one-way light travel time of up to 22 minutes, preventing real-time joystick control from Earth.

title: Perseverance Jezero Lander
subtitle: Mars Atmospheric Entry, Descent & Touchdown
analogue: NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance & Curiosity Sky Crane
briefing: Execute interplanetary cruise to Mars, withstand atmospheric entry deceleration, deploy a supersonic parachute within the aerodynamic stability window, and fire pulsed retro-rockets to touch down in Jezero Crater.
requirementsList: Interplanetary Trans-Mars Injection Delta-V Capacity
Pulsed High-Thrust Retro-Rocket Propulsion for Terminal Deceleration
Reinforced Landing Gear with High Shock Stroke Absorption
Thermal Control and Autonomous Safing for 12.5-min Light Delay
realWorldContext: Known as the 'Seven Minutes of Terror', Mars entry requires automated sequence execution as radio signals take over 10 minutes to reach Earth.

title: DAVINCI+ Venus Atmospheric Probe
subtitle: Super-Critical CO2 Atmosphere & Acid Cloud Sounding
briefing: Traverse to the inner solar system, enter high-inclination orbit around Venus, and plunge through corrosive sulfuric acid cloud layers to analyze atmospheric chemistry and surface geology.
requirementsList: Thermal Protection for Extreme 2,600 W/m² Solar Irradiance
Radiation-Hardened Avionics for Inner Solar Flare Transits
High-Frequency X/Ka Band Telemetry to Pierce Dense Atmosphere
Synthetic Aperture Radar for Cloud-Piercing Surface Mapping
realWorldContext: Venus boasts a runaway greenhouse effect generating surface temperatures of 465°C and atmospheric pressures 92 times greater than Earth.

title: Europa Clipper Astrobiology Reconnaissance
subtitle: Jovian Radiation Belt Infiltration & Cryovolcanic Sounding
briefing: Embark on an outer solar system voyage to Jupiter, perform gravity-assist maneuvers, and execute 40+ low-altitude flybys of ice-covered moon Europa inside Jupiter's lethal radiation belts.
requirementsList: High-Energy Deep-Space Propulsion (TMI / Jupiter Capture)
Radiation-Hardened RAD750 Flight Computer with Heavy Vault Shielding
Ice-Penetrating Radar Sounder for Subsurface Ocean Detection
Massive Power Generation at 5.2 AU (Nuclear MMRTG or Giant Arrays)
realWorldContext: Europa harbors a global saltwater ocean beneath its icy crust with more liquid water than all of Earth's oceans combined.

title: Dragonfly Titan Atmospheric Explorer
subtitle: Methane Seas Exploration & Prebiotic Chemistry
briefing: Journey across 1.4 billion kilometers to Saturn's giant moon Titan, enter its cryogenic nitrogen atmosphere, and operate an autonomous exploration platform across methane dunes and seas.
requirementsList: Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (MMRTG) Power
Autonomous Flight Software for 80-minute One-Way Light Delay
Cryogenic Thermal Insulation for -179°C Surface Temperature
Large-Aperture High-Gain Antenna for Deep Space Comms Link
realWorldContext: Titan has a dense atmosphere (1.5x Earth pressure) and low gravity (0.14g), making aerial flight and exploration uniquely feasible.

title: OSIRIS-REx Bennu Sample Return
subtitle: Near-Earth Asteroid Proximity Operations & Sample Retrieval
briefing: Rendezvous with near-Earth carbonaceous asteroid Bennu, conduct microgravity proximity orbital surveys, execute a Touch-And-Go sample collection, and deliver the return capsule back to Earth.
requirementsList: Precision Micro-Impulse Propulsion for Micro-g Navigation
Flash LIDAR Hazard Mapping for Rugged Boulder Rubble Fields
High-Gain Optical / Radio Comms for Fine Trajectory Reconstruction
Earth Return Trajectory Delta-V Budget
realWorldContext: Bennu is a rubble-pile asteroid composed of rock, gravel, and organic carbon compounds dating back to the formation of the Solar System 4.5 billion years ago.
